speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Since this is an infant, I will be asking their caregiver questions. Can you tell me the infant's age and exactly what activities trigger these episodes of stridor and wheezing?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The combination of stridor and wheezing exacerbated by crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting in a 10-month-old, is classic for this condition, likely complicated by aspiration or gastroesophageal reflux.
